thread.title: Election Results Confirm Stock Rally; Twilio, CyberArk, Ulta, Humana Hot; Square, Activision Not | Investor's Business Daily

author: IBD STAFF
title: Election Results Confirm Stock Rally; Twilio, CyberArk, Ulta, Humana Hot; Square, Activision Not | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market rally had a follow-through day Wednesday following midterm election results. The Dow Jones, S&P 500 index and Nasdaq composite rallied, though techs in particular pulled back late in the week. Twilio ( TWLO ), CyberArk Software ( CYBR ), Planet Fitness ( PLNT ) and Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) reported strong earnings or guidance, sending their stocks above buy points, at least briefly. But Square ( SQ ), Trade Desk ( TTD ), Activision Blizzard ( ATVI ) were among notable earnings losers. The Federal Reserve took no action, but a December Fed rate hike is expected.
X Stock Rally Confirmed, More Leaders Break Out Wall Street cheered election results that left the GOP holding the Senate but Democrats retaking the House. Health insurers and marijuana stocks were big winners. The Dow Jones, S&P 500 index and Nasdaq confirmed a new stock market uptrend Wednesday with powerful, high-volume gains clearing key technical levels. Stocks pulled back late in the week, especially techs. For the week, the Dow rose 2.8%, the S&P 500 2.1% and the Nasdaq just 0.7%. A growing number of leading stocks broke out of bases, including several on earnings reports or guidance. Some faltered Friday. Crude oil prices continued to fall, dropping below $60 intraday Friday. Treasury yields tested recent highs.
Twilio Headlines Software Winners Twilio ( TWLO ) reported a surprise profit while revenue growth soared 68%, its fourth straight quarter of acceleration. The communications software make guided high for Q4. Twilio's core product has been a software platform that app developers use for text messaging and other communications. Twilio in October agreed to buy mass-email platform SendGrid ( SEND ) for $2 billion. Twilio stock skyrocketed.
CyberArk Software ( CYBR ) earnings shot up 92%, accelerating for a third quarter, as the cybersecurity firm guided high on Q4. Analysts said sales execution has improved. CyberArk rose jumped 8.8% Thursday, briefly clearing a buy point and hitting a record high.
Tableau Software ( DATA ) reported a smaller-than-expected loss while sales came in light. But investors focused on fiscal 2019 guidance for 20% revenue growth under new accounting rules as the data analytics software maker shifts to a subscription model. Tableau stock shot up to a multiyear high.
Five9 ( FIVN ) adjusted profit shot up 350% as revenue rose 30%, both well above views. The maker of business software for call-center communications cited continued momentum in the enterprise business.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Planet Fitness Muscles To New High Planet Fitness ( PLNT ) earnings vaulted 47% to 28 cents a share, beating views. Revenue jumped 40% to $137 million, the best sales gain in more than four years. The IBD 50 stock topped a 55.45 buy point. The low-fee gym operator sees full-year adjusted EPS up 43% and revenue up 33%. Analysts had expected a 34.5% EPS gain with sales rising about 27%.
Payment Stocks Diverge On Earnings Square ( SQ ) Q3 earnings rose 86% as revenue swelled 68 to $431, both topping expectations. But higher product investments as well as costs tied to integrating acquired companies are pressuring margins. The digital payment processor guided low on Q4 profit. EVO Payments ( EVOP ) reported an 89% gain while revenue rose 9%, both beating, in its second report since a May IPO. Green Dot Payments ( GDOT ), which offers reloadable prepaid debit cards, announced a 74% adjusted EPS gain on solid sales growth. Worldpay ( WP ) narrowly topped EPS views while revenue was in line. Square stock plunged Thursday while EVO Payments and Green Dot both cleared buy points Thursday, but pulled back below those entries by Friday's close. Worldpay fell.
These Payment Stocks Are Sitting On A $1 Trillion Opportunity
Keurig Tops, Monster Fight With Coke Coffee-and-soda company Keurig Dr Pepper ( KDP ) saw EPS slide 73% to, despite sales soaring 64% to $2.86 billion. Keurig stock rallied, making a new high Thursday. Monster Beverage EPS jumped 25% as sales climbed 12% to $1.02 billion. But the energy-drink maker fell Thursday on news that distribution partner Coca-Cola ( KO ) plans Coke-branded energy drinks. Coca-Cola owns a sizable stake in Monster Beverage and takeover buzz had resurfaced over the summer.
Amazon: King Of Queens? Amazon reportedly selected the Long Island City neighborhood in Queens, N.Y., as the second location for a second headquarters, dubbed HQ2, in addition to the Crystal City area of Arlington, Va. That would end a yearlong search by Amazon. The e-commerce giant is also now offering free shipping with no purchase minimum for the first time this holiday season.
Health Insurers Soar On Election Results, Humana Election results were good for Wall Street and great for the Medical-Managed Care industry group, while a big earnings beat for Humana ( HUM ) added some sparkle. Humana earnings leapt 35% to $4.58 per share, 29 cents ahead of the analyst consensus. Revenue rose 7% to $14.2 billion, clearing estimates of $13.9 billion. The senior-focused insurer bumped predicted strong individual Medicare Advantage growth.
The Democratic takeover of the House likely ends any legislative efforts to curb ObamaCare. Medicaid expansion initiatives passed in Idaho, Nebraska and Utah. With Democrat Laura Kelly winning the Kansas gubernatorial race, Medicaid could expand there too.
Humana stock vaulted 6.7% Wednesday, clearing a buy point at 341.40 on UnitedHealth ( UNH ), Anthem ( ANTM ) and Cigna ( CI ) also hit buying opportunities on Wednesday. Medicaid-focused insurers Centene ( CNC ) and Molina Healthcare ( MOH ) shot up 9.2% and 10.5%, respectively, on Wednesday.
Etsy Earnings, Guidance Strong The e-commerce dealer of arts and crafts crashed Q3 earnings estimates and raised full-year guidance for revenue and for gross merchandise sales. Etsy ( ETSY ) also OK'd a $200 million buyback. Etsy stock soared.
Disney Growth Improves; Iger Lays Out Streaming Plans Disney ( DIS ) topped estimates with 38% and 12% EPS and revenue growth to $1.48 and $14.31 billion, respectively. The 21st Century Fox ( FOXA ) asset acquisition and direct-to-consumer streaming platforms will be a focus in 2019, said CEO Bob Iger. The Disney-branded streaming platform, coming late 2019, will be called "Disney Plus," or Disney+, and will feature "Star Wars: Rogue One" and "Avengers" spinoff series. Iger alluded to future investment in Hulu, and said the new theme parks' "Star Wars" lands will be the biggest lands ever built. Meanwhile, 21st Century Fox logged 6% EPS growth to 52 cents and 2.5% revenue gains to $7.18 billion, missing views.
Disney stock, a Dow Jones component, closed right on its 118 buy point Friday.
Ulta Beauty Breaks Out On its investor day, retailer Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) lifted the bottom end of comparable sales guidance; it now expects 7%-8% comps vs. prior outlook for 6%-8%. It also reiterated previous outlook for low 20s percentage EPS growth, and said it sees 5%-7% comps and mid- to high-teens percentage range EPS in fiscal 2019, 2020, and 2021. After taking an initial hit, shares surged past a 290.40 buy point and easily cleared the 300 price level. Separately, value cosmetics brand Elf Beauty ( ELF ) beat estimates late Monday with flat EPS of 17 cents, surprising analysts who had expected a decline. Sales fell 11% to $64 million, also topping. And early shipment of holiday products to Target ( TGT ) helped sales. Elf lifted the lower end of profit guidance.
Fed Stands Pat, Sticks With Rate Hike Path The Fed surprised no one by leaving its key interest rate unchanged Thursday with a statement that did little to diminish high odds of another rate hike in December. The Fed downplayed the slowdown in business spending, didn't mention the recent stock-market correction and maintained its $50 billion monthly pace of balance sheet shrinkage. After the meeting, the 2-year Treasury yield briefly hit a new post-crisis high of 2.97%, while the dollar staged a rebound.
Activision, Take-Two Gloomy On Holidays Activision Blizzard ( ATVI ) and Take-Two Interactive Software ( TTWO ) followed video game peer Electronic Arts ( EA ) in forecasting lower-than-expected December-quarter figures. Activision and Take-Two delivered generally upbeat September-quarter results, but both stocks fell sharply. Both recently released big games for the large installed base of current-generation game consoles. Activision's "Call of Duty: Black Ops 4" and Take-Two's "Red Dead Redemption 2" are already among the year's top-selling games.
Drug Earnings Endo International ( ENDP ), Horizon Pharma ( HZNP ) and Mallinckrodt ( MNK ) topped views, but IBD 50 stock Jazz Pharmaceuticals ( JAZZ ) lagged sales and guidance expectations. Endo stock crumbled on its plans for a weaker-than-expected cellulite treatment. Horizon Pharma stock broke out. Eli Lilly ( LLY ) adjusted profit of $1.39 per share topped, but $6.06 billion in sales were slightly short. Shares were volatile. AstraZeneca ( AZN ) revenue of $5.34 billion beat some views and missed others, while core earnings of 71 cents per share easily beat, prompting a breakout. Jazz had a mixed quarter with adjusted profit of $3.58 per share coming in north of views, while $469.4 million in sales lagged. Mylan reported adjusted income of $1.25 per share, topping estimates, while sales of $2.86 billion were light.
Biotech Earnings Regeneron Pharmaceuticals ( REGN ) and Vanda Pharmaceuticals ( VNDA ) topped third-quarter expectations last week. Regeneron came in with $1.663 billion in sales and earnings of $5.87 per share, excluding items. Both metrics rose by double-digit percentages. But Regeneron cut its outlook for full-year collaboration revenue from partner Sanofi. Vanda broke out Thursday after adjusted profit of 20 cents per share on $49.1 million in sales beat consensus expectations.
News In Brief Alarm.com ( ALRM ) earnings and revenue topped Q3 estimates and the cloud security company issued December quarter guidance above expectations. Video camera sales boosted results. Alarm.com's biggest customers are companies that sell alarm-monitoring services. Shares soared Thursday but wiped out those gains Friday.
II-VI ( IIVI ) will buy Finisar ( FNSR ) in a cash-and-stock deal initially worth $3.2 billion, or $26 per Finisar share. Both are Apple 3D sensor suppliers. Apple ( AAPL ) took a stake in Finisar last year.
Match Group ( MTCH ) topped Q3 views but said Q4 subscriber growth for mobile dating app Tinder will slow quarter-over-quarter and its December-quarter revenue outlook was light. Match plans a national ad campaign for Tinder. Match also plans a special $560 million dividend of which 80% will go to parent IAC/Interactive. Match stock plunged.
Fabrinet ( FN ), a contract manufacturer specializing in optical products, vaulted 11% on a beat-and-raise fiscal first quarter. Manufacturing is moving outside China due to Trump tariffs. Fabrinet, which has a manufacturing plant in Thailand, should get a boost, one analyst said.
Trade Desk ( TTD ) reported Q3 earnings of 65 cents a share, up 86% from a year ago, with revenue rising 50% to $118.8 million, topping analyst estimates. The provider of automated advertising buying tools forecast Q4 revenue of $147 million, just above estimates of $144.7 million. Trade Desk stock tumbled early Friday but eked out a small gain by the close.
Genomic Health ( GHDX ) stock rocketed after the diagnostics firm reported $101.3 million in sales and adjusted profit of 35 cents per share, topping expectations for $94 million and 7 cents, respectively.
Boeing ( BA ) released a warning to pilots on how to deal with faulty readings from a key sensor on new 737 Max planes, which could cause the planes to dive. The FAA made it mandatory for pilots to follow the warning. That comes after a Lion Air jet crashed shortly after take-off from Indonesia on Oct. 29. The cause hasn't been determined but black box data found that the 737 Max had problems with airspeed on prior flights.
Wireless network gear maker CommScope ( COMM ) agreed to buy cable set-top box maker Arris ( ARRS ) in a $7.4 billion merger that combines a wireless network gear maker with a cable equipment provider. CommScope stock plunged on the deal announcement. The Carlyle Group will invest $1 billion in CommScope to provide financing for the deal.
Bojangles ( BOJA ), the Southern-themed restaurant chain, said it would be bought in an all-cash transaction, which would total about $594 million, by the investment firms Durational Capital Management and the Jordan Co.
Shares of Booking Holdings ( BKNG ), formerly known as Priceline, jumped after it reported third-quarter results that fell short on earnings but showed improved performance in some segments. TripAdvisor ( TRIP ) popped on its Q3 results.
Crocs ( CROX ) charged past a buy point after it reported better-than-expected Q3 earnings. The strong showing helped the comfy footwear specialist reach a seven-year high.
Zebra Technologies ( ZBRA ) reported better-than-expected sales and earnings for the third quarter thanks to strong demand for its enterprise asset tracking systems. The news pushed its stock to record heights.
Roku ( ROKU ) fell sharply after the streaming video platform reported decelerating growth in the third quarter. Roku also is facing new competition in streaming hardware from cable giant Comcast ( CMCSA ).
CVS Health ( CVS ) reported EPS of $1.73, up 15% and 2 cents ahead of estimates. Revenue growth of 2.4% to $47.269 billion also topped estimates. Growth of 0.8% in same-store sales for front-of-store merchandise reversed a 1% decline in Q2. CVS stock jumped Tuesday on earnings, then briefly cleared a buy point Wednesday on election results. CVS will soon close its Aetna ( AET ) acquisition.
